newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to submit 98 budget to Duma at end August.
newsitem.headline: Russia to submit 98 budget to Duma at end August.

text.p: The Russian government plans to submit its draft 1998 budget to parliament at the end of August, First Deputy Finance Minister Vladimir Petrov said on Thursday.
"We will present the budget to the government again on August 10 so as to submit it to (parliament) at the end of August," Petrov told a news briefing.

Petrov said the 1998 budget deficit, according to international standards which include debt financing, would be 4.6 percent of gross domestic product. The total 1997 budget deficit by international standards is seven percent of GDP.

First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais has said the 1998 deficit would be five percent of GDP, comprising a primary deficit excluding borrowing costs of 0.5 percent and 4.5 percent on debt servicing.

The government is pushing parliament to pass a new tax code, which it says is crucial to ending the crisis in state finances and on which the 1998 budget is based, before it recesses for the summer in three weeks.

But the government faces stiff opposition from deputies over the code, as well as over its proposals to cut spending by one fifth under the 1997 budget, which the State Duma lower house of parliament will consider next week.
